ai.description: This large turtle reaches 60 cm in carapace length. It features an olive-green shell with yellow-rimmed ocelli and a distinct yellow patch on the head. The snout is tubular and the plastron is white.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Nilssonia hurum* is best distinguished by the four to eight distinct, eye-like ocelli (yellow-ringed black spots) present on the dorsal carapace of juveniles and adults.
ai.habitat: The Indian Peacock Softshell Turtle inhabits deep, slow-moving rivers, streams, and ponds with soft, muddy bottoms and sparse aquatic vegetation, typically below 500m.
ai.behavior: The Indian Peacock Softshell Turtle is primarily diurnal, often basking on riverbanks during the day before foraging for fish, crustaceans, and vegetation in the water.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nilssonia hurum* is oviparous, laying 15–30 spherical eggs in nests dug in sandbanks. Breeding occurs from December to March, peaking in the winter months.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Peacock Softshell Turtle is found across the Indo-Gangetic plains, primarily inhabiting the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Indus river systems in northern India.
